chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father Sayf, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, who said:

Some of our companions wrote, asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about certain matters, and instructed me to ask him about the right of the Muslim upon his brother. So I asked him, but he did not answer me. When I came to bid him farewell, I said, 'I asked you, but you did not answer me.' He said, 'I fear that you will be disbelieving. Indeed, among the most difficult of what Allah has imposed upon His creatures are three: The fairness of a man towards himself, until he is pleased for his brother from himself only with what he is pleased for his own self from him; and the sharing of wealth with the brother; and the remembrance of Allah in every state—not merely saying 'Glory be to Allah' and 'Praise be to Allah', but when Allah prohibits something for him, he leaves it.'

key_terms.إِنْصَافَ الْمَرْءِ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: Fairness of the man from himself
key_terms.حَقِّ الْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى أَخِيهِ: Right of the Muslim upon his brother
key_terms.ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: Remembrance of Allah in every state

ai.seo_question: What are the three most difficult rights of the Muslim upon his brother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reveals that these three rights are among the most difficult obligations because they require internalizing justice and constant mindfulness beyond mere ritual. The emphasis on 'self-fairness' (insaf al-nafs) aligns with the Shia concept of *nafs* purification, while linking remembrance (*dhikr*) to abstaining from prohibitions reflects the Quranic principle that true piety is measured by avoiding sin. This hadith serves as a practical guide for believers to integrate spiritual consciousness into daily social and financial interactions.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Sayf, from his father Sayf, from his father Sayf, from Abdul A’ala Bin Ayn who said,

‘Some of our companions wrote asking Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about certain things, and instructed me that I ask him<sup>asws</sup> about the right of the Muslim upon his brother. So I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, but he<sup>asws</sup> did not answer me. So when I went over to bid farewell to him<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘I did ask you<sup>asws</sup>, but you<sup>asws</sup> did not answer me’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> feared that you would be disbelieving. From the most difficult of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Imposed upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures are three – The fairness of the man from himself until he is not pleased for his brother from himself except with what he is pleased for his own self from him, and equalisation of the brother in the wealth, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon every state, not being (the saying of) ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is due to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, but during what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Prohibited upon him, he leaves it’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Sayf from his father, Sayf from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ ibn ‘A’Yun who has said the following:

“Once certain individual of our people wrote to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) asking him about certain issues and they ordered me to ask the Imam about the rights of the Muslim on his Muslim brother and I asked the Imam but he did not answer me. When I went to say farewell to him I said, ‘I asked you that question but you did not answer me.’ The Imam said, ‘I am afraid you may disregard them. Of the obligations most pressing that Allah has made obligatory upon His creature are three things: a man’s yielding to justice against his own soul so as not to accept for his brother (in belief) what he does not accept for his own self, to assist his brother with his property and speak of Allah in all conditions. I do not mean thereby, saying, ‘Glory belongs to Allah and all praise belongs to Allah. Truly speaking of and remembering Allah is to stay away from whatever He has prohibited.’”
